title: Probe illegal online advertising by betting centers
byline: Committee on Public Finance (COPF) has directed the Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (TRC) and other relevant institutions to carry out a probe on illegal online advertising by betting centres, it was revealed yesterday.

title: Hospitals under pressure as Dengue cases spike
byline: Health authorities have raised concerns that Sri Lanka’s healthcare system could come under severe pressure if the current rise in dengue admissions continues.

title: Open letter from Rosy Senanayake to the Government of Sri Lanka
byline: Former Colombo Mayor and former Member of Parliament Rosy Senanayake has issued an open letter calling for urgent action to address what she describes as a deepening child protection crisis in Sri Lanka, urging both domestic and international authorities to intervene.

title: Soft drinks, sedentary lifestyles fuel rise in childhood obesity
byline: Childhood obesity is increasing in Sri Lanka, with health authorities pointing to higher consumption of carbonated beverages and unhealthy lifestyles as key contributing factors.

title: Used vehicle prices could rise again after removal of 15% valuation reduction: VIASL
byline: The Vehicle Importers Association of Sri Lanka (VIASL) has warned that the prices of imported used vehicles could increase significantly following the removal of the 15 percent valuation reduction previously applied when determining the Customs value of used vehicles.

title: Sri Lanka launches export roadmap targeting US$ 36bn by 2030
byline: Sri Lanka yesterday unveiled an ambitious five-year export roadmap targeting annual export earnings of US$36 billion by 2030, as the government seeks to deepen the country’s post-crisis recovery by diversifying exports, expanding market access and addressing long-standing constraints that have limited competitiveness.

title: Build stronger export engine for lasting recovery: CBSL Governor
byline: Sri Lanka’s economic recovery will struggle to gain lasting momentum unless the country significantly expands its export base and improves access to trade finance, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe said yesterday, positioning export-led growth as the next critical phase of the country’s post-crisis rebuilding effort.

title: Manufacturing, services return to growth path in May
byline: Private sector activity regained momentum in May, with both manufacturing and services expanding after a softer April, although businesses remained wary of risks linked to the escalating conflict in the Middle East.

title: G7 vows new Russia sanctions amid optimism for Ukraine peace
byline: G7 leaders, such as German Chancellor Merz, are sounding more upbeat about the push for peace in Ukraine. The G7 is looking to hit Russia with new energy sanctions as the Strait of Hormuz is expected to reopen.

title: Rough seas, strong winds forecast for multi-day fishing boats
byline: The Meteorology Department has warned multi-day fishing vessels operating in Sri Lankan waters to exercise caution, as rough sea conditions and strong winds are expected over the next 24 hours.

title: Group planned to attack White House UFC event using snipers and drones, FBI says
byline: The FBI thwarted a plot targeting Sunday’s UFC event at the White House and has arrested five men, the US justice department said on Tuesday.

title: Messi scores hat-trick against Algeria in FIFA World Cup 2026 qualifiers
byline: Lionel Messi has completed a hat-trick against Algeria in Group ’J’ of the FIFA World Cup 2026 qualifiers. He gave Argentina a strong 3-0 lead in his first World Cup match with a hat-trick.

title: World crude oil prices ease below $80
byline: Global crude oil prices remained below the key US$80 per barrel mark on Wednesday, easing from recent highs as expectations of improved oil supply and easing geopolitical tensions weighed on the market.

title: Struggling Pizza Hut chain to be sold for $2.7bn
byline: Yum! Brands is selling its struggling Pizza Hut chain in a deal worth $2.7bn (£2bn), the company has announced.

title: No seat belts? don’t start the vehicle, warns Dilantha
byline: Renowned Sri Lankan racing driver Dilantha Malagamuwa has issued a strong warning to motorists, urging them to ensure that all passengers are wearing seat belts before starting their vehicles, as Sri Lanka prepares to strictly enforce mandatory seat belt regulations from June 20.

title: Transparency, regulations should be convincing; Indonesian envoy
byline: Indonesian Ambassador to Sri Lanka, Dewi Gustina Tobing was the latest foreign envoy to assert that transparency and regulations related to the investment climate in Sri Lanka should be convincing to the private sector.

title: Buckle up or face legal action
byline: Amid the increasing number of road accidents and fatalities, the National Council for Road Safety said that the mandatory use of seat belts by motorists and passengers will be strictly enforced from June 20, 2026.

title: Lion cub viewing at Dehiwala zoo ends June 21
byline: The public will have until June 21 to view the two newborn lion cubs at the Dehiwala Zoological Gardens, as the cubs will no longer be displayed after that due to safety concerns, Director General Chandana Rajapaksha said.

title: CID admits to stripping, conducting deep invasive search on Suresh Sallay, reveals wife
byline: Manori Sallay, the wife of former Director of the State Intelligence Service (SIS), Major General (Retired) Suresh Sallay, today alleged that the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has, for the first time, admitted to subjecting Suresh Sallay to a deeply invasive physical search.

title: Bribery Commission arrests Yoshitha over Navy probe
byline: Yoshitha Rajapaksa, the second son of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa, was arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) this morning (17) after appearing before the commission to provide a statement.

title: Cardinal Malcolm Ranjith never had prior knowledge on Easter Sunday attacks: Fr. Cyril Gamini
byline: The Archbishop of Colombo was never given prior warnings on the Easter Sunday bomb attacks and he was informed about the mayhem on April 21st morning after he held a private service at Bishops House Colombo, spokesman for Cardinal Ranjith, Fr. Cyril Gamini Fernando said today.

title: Sri Lanka unveils NEDP 2026–2030 aiming for US$ 36 billion export target
byline: The National Export Development Plan (NEDP) 2026–2030, launched in Colombo yesterday (16), sets a target of achieving US$ 36 billion in export earnings by 2030 while positioning Sri Lanka as a competitive, logistics- and knowledge-based export hub serving regional and global markets.

title: Serious shortage of essential and priority medicines in state hospitals – Health data shows
byline: According to official data from the Ministry of Health, there is a serious shortage of essential and priority medicines in the government health system.

title: Ministry introduces healthy school canteen guidelines
byline: The Health Ministry has introduced “Healthy School Canteen Guidelines,” which provide standards for school canteens, healthy food recipes, and lists of foods that should be avoided, as part of efforts to improve child nutrition in Sri Lanka

title: Sri Lanka loses Rs. 9.4bn in tobacco tax revenue amid shifting market trends - report
byline: Sri Lanka has recorded an estimated loss of Rs. 9.4 billion in tobacco tax revenue in 2024 due to changes in cigarette brand market shares following a 20% tax increase introduced in 2023, recent data cited by researchers at Verité Research said.

title: Gotabaya’s writ petition to be heard today
byline: The writ petition filed by former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa seeking an order preventing his arrest in connection with ongoing investigations into the 2019 Easter Sunday terror attacks is scheduled to be heard before the Court of Appeal today at 1.30 p.m.

title: Department of War restores U.S. Pacific Command designation
byline: The Department of War announced today that the U.S. Indo-Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM) will officially restore its name to the U.S. Pacific Command (USPACOM).

title: Iranian tankers exit U.S. blockade ahead of deal signing
byline: At least three Iranian tankers carrying nearly five million barrels of crude oil have exited the U.S. Navy blockade in the Strait of Hormuz in the first such outbound shipment in two months, as shipowners cautiously reposition ahead of a U.S.-Iran deal signing in Geneva on Friday.

title: Vegetable prices may rise further, farmers warn
byline: Vegetable prices across Sri Lanka are beginning to feel the pressure of a deepening crisis in the agricultural sector, with farmers warning that the situation could worsen sharply in the coming weeks.

title: Yoshitha Rajapaksa appears before Bribery Commission
byline: Yoshitha Rajapaksa, the son of former President Mahinda Rajapaksa, appeared before the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) this morning (17).

title: Israel launches fresh strikes on Lebanon despite Trump criticism
byline: Israeli forces have reportedly carried out new strikes in southern Lebanon despite renewed criticism from US President Donald Trump of Israel’s actions in the country.

title: Yoshitha Rajapaksa granted bail
byline: The Colombo Magistrate’s Court today (17) granted bail to Yoshitha Rajapaksa, hours after he was arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) in connection with an ongoing investigation into his recruitment to the Sri Lanka Navy.

title: Upcountry line train services to resume from Saturday
byline: Repair work on the damaged railway line between Nanu Oya and Ambewela on the Upcountry Line, which was affected by Cyclone Ditwah, has been completed, the Railway Department said.

title: Gotabaya’s writ petition fixed for tomorrow
byline: The writ petition filed by former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa seeking an order preventing his arrest in connection with the ongoing investigations into the 2019 Easter Sunday terror attacks was today fixed for tomorrow by the Court of Appeal.

title: Telegram challenges India ban over exam paper leak fears
byline: Telegram has taken the Indian government to court over its decision to temporarily ban the messaging platform days before millions of students retake a crucial medical entrance examination.

title: Foreign remittances up 32% in May
byline: Sri Lanka received US$847 million in workers’ remittances in May 2026, marking a 32% increase compared to the US$641.7 million received in May 2025, the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) said.

title: BCCI’s direct message to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after fight with Sri Lankan players: ’Media watch...’
byline: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has sent a clear and calm message to India A players, including teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, following an on-field altercation during the ongoing tri-series in Sri Lanka.

title: Rs. 1bn approved to upgrade school hostels
byline: The government has approved Rs. 1,008 million to repair and improve 126 school hostels across the country between 2026 and 2028, the Prime Minister’s Media Division said.

title: Iran sends tankers loaded with oil past US military blockade
byline: Three Iranian tankers loaded with crude oil have passed the US blockade line in the Gulf of Oman, ship-tracking data shows.

title: Sathosa reduces prices of essential goods islandwide
byline: Lanka Sathosa, the state-owned supermarket chain, has announced a reduction in prices of several essential consumer goods aimed at providing relief to the public.

title: ’I’m the boss’, Trump tells G7 counterparts
byline: ’’I’m the boss,’’ Trump said as he strode in to the morning session of the last day of the three-day G7 summit, with the other leaders already in their seats.

title: India 'A' power into Tri-Series Final
byline: India ’A’ bounced back from their Super Over loss to Sri Lanka ’A’ by defeating Afghanistan ’A’ by 101 runs and booking their place in the tri-series final.

title: Profit-taking erases early gains as market ends mixed; banking sector leads activity
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange ended Wednesday’s session on a mixed note, as early buying momentum faded amid profit-taking activity. The market opened positively, with the ASPI climbing to an intraday high of 93 points during early trading, reflecting improved investor sentiment and increased market volatility.

title: Expressway seat belt rule: Grace period ends June 19
byline: The three-month grace period granted for the implementation of mandatory seat belt regulations will end on June 19, after which legal action will be taken against motorists and passengers who fail to comply, the Transport, Highways and Urban Development Ministry said.

title: Norway’s crown princess undergoes successful lung transplant, palace says
byline: Norway’s Crown Princess Mette-Marit has undergone a successful lung transplant in Oslo, the country’s royal household has said.

title: No room for fuel price cut despite global price drop: Govt.
byline: Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando said the government is currently unable to reduce domestic fuel prices despite the decline in global fuel prices, as Sri Lanka is still using fuel stocks purchased at higher prices.

title: Petition to prevent elephant electrocutions fixed for hearing
byline: A petition seeking urgent action to prevent the electrocution and illegal killing of elephants was taken up before the Court of Appeal today, with the court fixing a date for the hearing and directing the respondent state institutions to file their objections.

title: Woman found dead inside parked vehicle near Teldeniya hospital
byline: The body of a woman was found inside a vehicle parked near Teldeniya Hospital today.

title: When you’re that rich, you can speak that low...” Trump jokes with UAE president
byline: US President Donald Trump shared a light-hearted moment with UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan during the G7 Summit in France, drawing laughter with remarks about the Emirati leader’s soft-spoken style.

title: Economy moving as planned, says deputy Finance Minister
byline: Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando yesterday expressed confidence that Sri Lanka’s economy remains on course to achieve its medium-term growth targets, citing the country’s 5.1% economic growth in the first quarter of 2026 as a positive indicator.

title: Trump threatens to resume bombing campaign if Iran does not ’’behave’’
byline: U.S President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that an ​interim accord with Iran was not final, and that ‌he could resume a bombing campaign if he did not like it or if Tehran did not ’’behave’’.

title: DVT emerging as ‘silent killer’ among young due to sedentary lifestyles, doctors warn
byline: A growing sedentary lifestyle among young people is increasingly being linked to a higher risk of Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT), a condition medical experts describe as a “silent killer” due to its sudden and often undetected onset.
